text:
devon: alert — edge NAT in us-west-2 showing ephemeral port exhaustion, started ~2026-03-18T06:12Z. dozens of model-puller pods returning connect errors to S3 and model registry. seeing surge in short-lived outbound connections.
ops-bot: [ALERT] NAT_EPHEMERAL_PORTS_LOW region=us-west-2 threshold=90% current=96%
maria: copying logs. noticed a big burst of concurrent model pulls from canary rollout ~06:10. could be the trigger.
chris: confirmed from perf dashboard — model-puller concurrency jumped 8x for ~90s. SYN retries spiked, TCP TIME_WAIT counts high on natgw.
samir: can we confirm conntrack / TIME_WAIT numbers from the proxies? run: `kubectl -n infra exec -it sidecar-proxy -- ss -tan | grep TIME-WAIT | wc -l`
liz: ran it on one proxy pod: `ss -tan | grep TIME-WAIT | wc -l` -> 142300. conntrack list showing ~220k entries on the node.
devon: logs show errors: `dial tcp 52.216.12.34:443: socket: too many open files` and `connect: no buffer space available`. natgw metrics: ActiveTCPConnections/Second doubled.
maria: immediate mitigations we can try in order: 1) scale up NAT capacity (add nat instances or additional nat gateways), 2) flip model-puller rollout to serialized pulls (reduce parallel fetches), 3) enable S3 VPC endpoint for registry traffic, 4) deploy sidecar keepalive patch to reuse sockets. which is fastest?
chris: fastest is toggling the rollout throttle and enabling VPC endpoint (if not already). provisioning another NAT GW takes ~5-10m and might not stop current TIME_WAIT tail.
samir: sidecar keepalive patch is ready (PR #4121) — it changes envoy config to long-lived upstream connections + connection pool. rollout could be done as a rapid canary.
liz: FYI we also have a leaky code path in model fetcher that spawns one goroutine per shard without reusing HTTP client. opened issue infra#889. short-term we can reduce replica concurrency env var `MODEL_FETCH_PARALLELISM` from 16->4.
devon: doing MODEL_FETCH_PARALLELISM=4 for canary namespace now. rolling back the canary rollout (pause) as well.
ops-bot: [ACTION] infra-oncall assigned to escalate NAT capacity with cloud team.
infra-oncall: pinging cloud provider support for soft limit bump and provisioning a second NAT gateway in us-west-2 now. ETA ~8 minutes.
maria: adding S3 VPC endpoint in the VPC (policy limited to model-registry S3 prefixes). starting creation — should be quick.
chris: also enabling ip_local_port_range tweak on nodes to expand ephemeral range as a temporary measure: `sysctl -w net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range=\"15000 61000\"` — but note AWS NAT mapping still constrained by source ports per egress IP.
samir: after keepalive sidecar rollout and MODEL_FETCH_PARALLELISM throttle, connection churn dropped sharply in a small test. recommend patch rollout across edge proxies after NAT capacity stabilized.
liz: actionable runbook entry -> if ephemeral ports > 180k across NAT gateway and 5xx% > 5% for 3m: 1) pause rollouts that spike pulls, 2) create S3 VPC endpoint, 3) apply sidecar keepalive, 4) provision extra NAT gateway or instances, 5) consider NAT pool IP expansion.
devon: tracking: paused canary, set MODEL_FETCH_PARALLELISM=4, S3 endpoint request in progress, sidecar keepalive canary deploy in 3m, cloud provisioning for second NAT gw requested.
maria: cloud team says second NAT gw created and attached, route table updated. early metrics: ephemeral port utilization dropping from 96% -> 68%. 5xxs from model-pull dropped to baseline.
chris: follow-up tasks: 1) merge sidecar keepalive PR and rollout on a rolling window with traffic shaping, 2) add an automated circuit-breaker to pause high-concurrency model fetch rollouts, 3) document conntrack/TIME_WAIT thresholds in runbook.
samir: also propose we add pre-warm artifact cache on nodes to avoid parallel remote pulls during deploys. reduces egress rate by keeping copies locally.
liz: will add runbook changes and the post-incident blameless doc. tagging infra-postmortems. :memo: :thumbsup:
devon: great work team — keeping this thread open for the postmortem. will update when sidecar merge and rollout complete.
